transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. We've got the 48-hour water conservation restriction from the municipal authority, and I need to put together a water-control plan before we proceed. I know we've got 2,400 liters in the reclaimed-water tank, and both Line X and Line Y are scheduled to run during the restriction. Before I make any final decisions on process-water allocation, let's go through our routine conservation huddle updates. Could I hear from Quality, Maintenance, and EHS on anything relevant to our water usage during this period?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I have an important quality update. My lab test, completed this morning but not yet uploaded to the shared quality folder, found the reclaimed-water conductivity at 1,800 microsiemens per centimeter. Line X's process limit is 1,200, so the reclaimed water exceeds Line X's limit. Line Y's process limit is 2,200, and Line Y's scheduled batch requires exactly 1,800 liters, so the reclaimed water is acceptable for that batch — but only after a conductivity test is recorded.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I have a maintenance update. My inspection of the recovery skid, documented in my maintenance notebook but not yet entered in the work-order system, found that the skid requires an exact 3-hour membrane flush before use and can then deliver reclaimed water at no more than 600 liters per hour. This is critical for planning any additional reclaimed water supply during the restriction period.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I have an EHS update from my permit review with the municipal inspector yesterday. That review, which is awaiting attachment to the site's permit record, found that reclaimed water may be used only after its residual sanitizer is adjusted to exactly 0.3 parts per million, and that each use day requires a signed sanitizer log. This is a permit condition, so it applies to any reclaimed-water use during the restriction period.
transcript.speaker: A4

decisions.reclaimed_water_plan: Allocate 1,800 liters of reclaimed water to Line Y's scheduled batch. Do not use reclaimed water on Line X due to conductivity exceeding its process limit. If additional reclaimed water is needed, the recovery skid must undergo a 3-hour membrane flush before use and can deliver at no more than 600 liters per hour. Before any reclaimed water is used, residual sanitizer must be adjusted to exactly 0.3 ppm and a signed sanitizer log must be completed for each use day, and a conductivity test must be recorded.

commitments.detail: Ensure the reclaimed-water conductivity test result (1,800 µS/cm) is uploaded to the shared quality folder before Line Y's batch begins.
Enter the recovery skid inspection findings (3-hour membrane flush, 600 L/hr max delivery) into the work-order system.
Attach the EHS permit review findings to the site's permit record and ensure a signed sanitizer log is completed for each day reclaimed water is used.
Sign the water-control plan authorizing 1,800 liters of reclaimed water for Line Y only, with sanitizer adjusted to 0.3 ppm and conductivity test recorded prior to use.
